evidence.quote:
If I take it up I must understand every detail," said he.  "Take time
to consider.  The smallest point may be the most essential.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes states a methodical principle of attending to every small detail when investigating.

evidence.quote:
The words are
written with a broad-pointed, violet-tinted pencil of a not unusual
pattern.  You will observe that the paper is torn away at the side here
after the printing was done, so that the 's' of 'soap' is partly gone.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes makes detailed observations about the pencil and torn paper to draw inferences.

evidence.quote:
The matches have, of course, been
used to light cigarettes.  That is obvious from the shortness of the
burnt end.  Half the match is consumed in lighting a pipe or cigar.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes reasons from physical clues (burnt match length) to deduce their use.

evidence.quote:
I don't understand that.  I should say that only a clean-shaven man
could have smoked this.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes infers from the cigarette stub that a clean-shaven person smoked it, contradicting the description.

evidence.quote:
There seems no other way, and
fortunately we need concern ourselves with the one paper only.  Here
are the Daily Gazette extracts of the last fortnight.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes reasons out that communication must occur via newspaper advertisements and reviews the extracts.

evidence.quote:
This other, however, prints 'match' when it should have
been 'matches.'  I can imagine that the word was taken out of a
dictionary, which would give the noun but not the plural.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes deduces a substitution of lodgers from the grammatical error suggesting a non-English speaker using a dictionary.

evidence.quote:
A single flash--that is A, surely.  Now, then.  How many
did you make it?  Twenty.  So did I.  That should mean T.
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes decodes flashed signals letter by letter using a numeric cipher.

evidence.quote:
And not a very
obscure cipher, Watson," said he.  "Why, of course, it is Italian!  The
A means that it is addressed to a woman.  'Beware! Beware!  Beware!'
evidence.paraphrase: Holmes interprets the cipher as Italian, deducing the message and its intended recipient.

evidence.quote:
It frightens me, Mr. Holmes.  I
can't sleep for fright.
evidence.paraphrase: The landlady expresses fear and sleeplessness over the mysterious lodger.

evidence.quote:
I caught a glimpse of a dark, beautiful,
horrified face glaring at the narrow opening of the box-room.
evidence.paraphrase: The hidden lodger reacts with horror upon noticing the observers.

evidence.quote:
two men came up behind
him, threw a coat over his head, and bundled him into a cab that was
beside the curb.  They drove him an hour, and then opened the door and
shot him out.
evidence.paraphrase: Mr. Warren is abducted, driven off, and dumped, in a case of mistaken identity.

evidence.quote:
there was
outlined a fresh track of blood.  The red steps pointed towards us and
led away from an inner room
evidence.paraphrase: The investigators discover a bloody trail leading to an inner room.

evidence.quote:
from the centre of
his broad, brown, upturned throat there projected the white haft of a
knife driven blade-deep into his body.
evidence.paraphrase: The body of the giant is found stabbed to death with a knife.

evidence.quote:
she sprang
into the air with a cry of joy.  Round and round the room she danced,
her hands clapping, her dark eyes gleaming with delighted wonder
evidence.paraphrase: Emilia Lucca reacts with joyful relief and dancing at the sight of Gorgiano's corpse.

evidence.quote:
We fled together, were married at Bari, and sold my jewels to gain the
money which would take us to America.  This was four years ago, and we
have been in New York ever since.
evidence.paraphrase: The couple recounts fleeing Italy and relocating to America four years prior.

evidence.quote:
he would signal to me from a
certain window, but when the signals came they were nothing but
warnings
evidence.paraphrase: The wife explains the arrangement of window-flash signaling as their means of communication.
